job.title: Ideal, modelled and real
job.subtitle: The same circuit three ways: computed exactly, predicted under a noise model, and measured on {{backend}}.
job.missing: There is no such run, or it is not one you may read.
job.unavailable: This build has no server, so a stored hardware run cannot be loaded. Everything that runs in this tab still works.
job.circuitMissing: The circuit this run belongs to could not be loaded, so there is nothing to compare the device against.
job.simulating: Simulating the circuit to build the first two columns…
job.simulationFailed: The circuit could not be simulated in this tab, so only the device’s own counts are available.
job.circuitChanged: This circuit has been edited since this job was submitted, so the drawing on screen is not the program the device ran. The ideal and modelled columns are not shown: every figure on them would be a subtraction between two different circuits, printed where a statement about the hardware belongs. The device’s own answer is below, unchanged.

status.heading: Nothing to compare yet
status.SUBMITTED: The run has been created and is on its way to {{backend}}.
status.QUEUED: Waiting in {{backend}}’s queue. Real devices are shared, and a queue can be hours deep — nothing is lost by closing this page, and the result will be here when it lands.
status.CANCELLED: This run was cancelled before it produced a result.
status.FAILED: The run did not produce a result.

failure.heading: The run did not produce a result
failure.CREDENTIAL_MISSING: The credential this run was paying with has been deleted, so it could no longer be followed.
failure.CREDENTIAL_INVALID: The provider refused the API key. It may have expired or been revoked, or its instance may no longer be reachable.
failure.QUOTA_EXHAUSTED: The plan’s quantum time was spent. It returns when the period rolls over.
failure.PROVIDER_REFUSED: The provider rejected the program. That is about the circuit or the device, not about the key.
failure.PROVIDER_FAILED: The device ran the circuit and reported a failure.
failure.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE: The provider could not be reached. This one may work if it is run again.
failure.RESULT_UNREADABLE: The device finished and its answer could not be read. The quantum time was spent and the counts were lost.
failure.POLL_ABANDONED: This system stopped asking after waiting far longer than any queue should take. The job may still exist in the provider’s console.
failure.QUEUE_UNAVAILABLE: The run was recorded but could not be scheduled, so nothing ever asked the provider about it.
failure.unknown: The run failed for a reason this build does not have a name for: {{code}}.
failure.SUBMIT_ABANDONED: This system tried to send the circuit and never learned whether the provider accepted it, so it stopped rather than sending it again — a repeat would buy a second run on the device. Check the provider’s console before submitting another.

comparison.heading: The three distributions
comparison.lead: One track, three readings. The bar is the ideal probability, with its phasor and its hue; each tick is where one of the other two readings put that outcome, and the sliver between them is the difference — outside the bar for an outcome that gained, cut out of it for one that lost.

chart.heading: Ideal, modelled and measured, on one chart
chart.summary: Each bar is the ideal probability. The upper band of a bar is the noise model’s reading, the lower one is the device’s; a chart with only one band has no model beside it.
chart.tableCaption: One row per basis state: its ideal probability, the noise model’s, the device’s, and the difference each makes.

comparison.shotNote: The device’s column is {{shots}} shots, so every figure taken from it carries a sampling error of roughly {{typical}}. A difference smaller than that is not a difference.
comparison.modelMissing: No noise model ran beside this result, so the middle reading is absent and the chart carries two distributions rather than three.
comparison.modelVsDeviceMissing: The noise run was sampled rather than computed exactly, so it produced a tally of the outcomes it happened to visit rather than a distribution over all of them. Model against device needs the second, and is left out rather than reconstructed from the first.
comparison.modelVsDeviceLead: This is the number the third column is worth having for: it says how well the model predicted the machine, which neither of the other two figures can.
comparison.modelScopeNote: The model runs the circuit as it was drawn, with transmon-like coherence and gate errors. The device ran the transpiled program below, which has more gates in it — so the model is usually the optimistic one, and the gap between it and the third column is largely what the transpilation cost.

movement.none: Nothing moved: the device reproduced the ideal distribution exactly, which at any real shot count means the differences are smaller than the sampling error.
movement.gainOnly: {{state}} gained {{gain}} on the device, and nothing lost any.
movement.lossOnly: {{state}} lost {{loss}} on the device, and nothing gained any.
movement.both: On the device, {{lost}} lost the most, {{loss}}, and {{gained}} gained the most, {{gain}}.
movement.others: the outcomes the circuit never reaches

refused.heading: These cannot be drawn on one chart
refused.unmeasured-qubit: This circuit leaves at least one qubit unmeasured, so the device reports a summary of the state rather than the state itself. Laying one over the other would attribute the missing half to hardware error.
refused.unwritten-clbit: This circuit has a classical bit no measurement fills, so one column of the device’s answer is not an outcome of anything.
refused.repeated-qubit: This circuit ends with one qubit written into two classical bits, so a device’s bitstring does not name a single basis state.
refused.conditioned: This circuit has a gate that only runs for some shots, so no single ideal state describes what the device did. The counts are still a measurement of it; there is simply nothing to lay them over.
refused.mid-circuit-measurement: This circuit measures a qubit and then keeps working on it. The device collapsed that wire and carried on; an ideal simulation with the measurement removed would keep a superposition the real run never had, and the difference would look exactly like hardware error.
refused.note: The device’s own counts are shown below, unchanged.
refused.noCounts: The device finished and returned no shots at all. There is nothing to compare, and nothing was measured — which is itself worth knowing, because the run still spent quantum time.
refused.circuit-changed: The circuit was edited after this job was submitted, so there is no ideal state on this page that describes what the device ran.
refused.register-mismatch: The stored counts are not keyed by the classical register this job’s program declared, so they cannot be laid over the chart. They belong to a different run, or to a different build of this system.

comparison.modelScopeNoteNamed: The model runs the circuit as it was drawn, under the “{{profile}}” profile. The device ran the transpiled program below, which has more gates in it — so the model is usually the optimistic one, and the gap between it and the third column is largely what the transpilation cost.

device.heading: Where this came from
device.lead: A result from real hardware is a measurement of a physical object at a moment in time. These are that object and that moment.
device.queueNote: How long it waited is measured from this run’s own timestamps. The queue length shown next to a device is today’s, on a machine that has since run everything ahead of this job, so it is not the queue this result waited in.
device.calibrationNote: The qubits above were chosen from that calibration. A device is re-tuned about once a day, so an older calibration means the placement was made against a machine that had already drifted.

program.heading: What was drawn, and what ran
program.lead: A processor of this family has no Hadamard and no CNOT. Its gates are rz, sx, x, id, cz, rx and rzz, so every drawn gate becomes several — and each one is an opportunity for the state to decay. This is where the third column’s difference comes from.
program.growth_one: {{drawn}} drawn gate became {{executed}} on the device.
program.growth_other: {{drawn}} drawn gates became {{executed}} on the device.
program.growthNone: The device ran no more gates than were drawn, which happens when the circuit was already written in the machine’s own basis.

cost.heading: Not all of them cost the same
cost.note: A frame change is a relabelling in the control electronics: no pulse is played, so it takes no time and adds no error. A pulse is real microwave drive with a real error rate. An entangling gate is one to two orders of magnitude worse than a pulse, and on almost every circuit it is where the fidelity actually goes.

program.notFlat: The stored program contains gate definitions, which a submitted program never does. The counts above are calls rather than the operations behind them, and are therefore understated.
program.sourceNote: OpenQASM 3 over the device’s own qubits — $53 is physical qubit 53, not a wire in the drawing. This is the stored text, exactly as it was sent.
